questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: **PERSPICUOUS**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 (Clear)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"perspicuous"** refers to something that is clearly expressed or easily understood; lucid. (स्पष्ट रूप से समझने योग्य)
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher's explanation was so perspicuous that no student had any questions.
 
 
• **"Clear"** means easy to understand, not ambiguous or confusing. (साफ़, स्पष्ट)
 
 
• **Example:** The instructions on the package were clear, making assembly a breeze.
 
 
• Hence, the most appropriate synonym of **"perspicuous"** is **"clear"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 (Clear)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Confused** (उलझन में): Unable to think clearly or understand something.
 
 
• **Example:** She looked confused when I asked her about the new policy.
 
 
 
• **Precarious** (अनिश्चित): Not securely held or in position; dangerously likely to fall or collapse.
 
 
• **Example:** The ladder was placed in a precarious position, making it risky to climb.
 
 
 
• **Muddled** (घबराया हुआ): In a state of confusion or disorder.
 
 
• **Example:** His thoughts were so muddled that he couldn’t explain his point properly.

Cracks, corrosion, and spectral scaffolds do not degrade meaning; they transmute it, encoding absence as presence and entropy as 1. legibility__. These architectural residues defy the chronological hygiene of masterplans, offering instead a fugitive temporality...*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Monumentality** (विशालता): The quality of being massive or impressive in scale. This refers to physical size rather than the "meaning" or "readability" the sentence focuses on.

questions.question: What should come in the place of blank number (4)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**insurgent**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage personifies urban decay as a rebellious, active force that resists control ("resists romanticization," "confounds enclosure," "Gentrification cannot domesticate it").
 
• Just before the blank, decay is described as "mutinous" (rebellious) and "mnemonic" (relating to memory). Furthermore, the author earlier refers to these spaces as sites of "interpretive insurgency."
 
• The word "**insurgent**" means rising in active revolt or rebellion. It perfectly aligns with the theme of ruins acting as a rebellious disruption against the city's attempt to erase or ignore them ("municipal forgetting").
 
• The other options do not fit: "syntactic" is redundant next to the word "syntax," "ornamental" contradicts the author's explicit rejection of beautification ("rendering disorder decorative"), and "equivocal" lacks the aggressive, resistant tone established by the word "mutinous."

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Yet decay resists even romanticization. It is not allegory, but ontic excess—a surplus that confounds enclosure. Gentrification cannot domesticate it; nostalgia cannot vitrify it. It lingers, mutinous and mnemonic, as an 4. insurgent__ syntax etched across municipal forgetting.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Syntactic** (वाक्य-विन्यास संबंधी): Relating to the rules of syntax or the arrangement of words. Using the phrase "syntactic syntax" would be highly repetitive and illogical here.
 
• **Ornamental** (सजावटी): Serving or intended as an ornament; decorative. This directly contradicts the passage's argument against aestheticizing decay.
 
• **Equivocal** (अस्पष्ट/गोलमोल): Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous. While ruins are complex, this word misses the active, rebellious nature of the decay being described.

questions.question: **Select the correct option**: Hardly had the meeting begun ___ the auditors demanded additional documentation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**when**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"when"** is used to indicate that one event occurred immediately after another.
 
• In this sentence, the use of **"when"** creates the correct meaning: the auditors demanded additional documentation right after the meeting began.
 
• Options **2 (than)**, **3 (before)**, and **4 (as)** are incorrect as they do not fit the grammatical structure and meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Hardly had the meeting begun **when**__ the auditors demanded additional documentation."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "than"** is incorrect because "than" is used for comparisons, not for indicating sequential actions.
 
• **Option 3: "before"** is incorrect because it implies one event happened earlier, which changes the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4: "as"** is incorrect because it suggests simultaneous actions, which does not align with the sentence structure.

questions.question: **Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:** The auditorium is spacious and can accommodate (1)/ large number of participants (2)/ for the seminar on rural banking (3)/ being held next week. (4)/

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the phrase "**large number of participants**."
 
• The term "**large number**" should be corrected to "**a large number**" to include the appropriate article.
 
• In English grammar, countable nouns such as "number" require an article to make the phrase grammatically correct.
 
• Thus, the correct phrase should be "**a large number of participants**."
 
• This error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The auditorium is spacious and can accommodate **a large number** of participants for the seminar on rural banking being held next week."*

• **Part 3: "for the seminar on rural banking"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 4: "being held next week."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
</ul

questions.question: **Change the following from active to passive**: Editors deem such practices incompatible with editorial ethics.

options.text: Such practices are deemed incompatible with editorial ethics.
Editorial ethics deems such practices as incompatible.
Editors have deemed editorial ethics incompatible with such practices.
Editorial compatibility is deemed absent in such practices.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Editors deem such practices incompatible with editorial ethics."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "such practices" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "deem" to "are deemed" (present simple passive).
 
• Add the rest of the sentence "incompatible with editorial ethics" as it is.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"Such practices are deemed incompatible with editorial ethics."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"Editorial ethics deems such practices as incompatible." – This is in active voice, not passive.
 
• **Option 3: **"Editors have deemed editorial ethics incompatible with such practices." – This is in active voice and does not follow the passive structure.

questions.question:

The changes must have been implemented without consulting the advisory board.

options.text: They must implement the changes without consulting anyone.

questions.solution:

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The subject of the passive sentence becomes the object of the active sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The changes must have been implemented without consulting the advisory board."
 
• To convert to active voice: Identify the implied subject (someone) who performed the action.
 
• Rewrite the sentence: "Someone must have implemented the changes without consulting the advisory board."
 
• Ensure that the meaning remains consistent with the original passive sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Someone must have implemented the changes without consulting the advisory board."*

• **Option 1: **"They must implement the changes without consulting anyone." – Incorrect as it changes the context by introducing "anyone" instead of "the advisory board."
 
• **Option 2: **"The advisory board must not have been consulted during changes." – Incorrect as it remains in passive voice.
 
• **Option 4: **"The changes must be implemented without advisory consultation." – Incorrect as it remains in passive voice.

questions.question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

She said, "I had already finished the work."

options.text: She said she already finished the work.
She said that she had already finished the work.
She said she has already finished the work.
She said that she would finish the work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she had already finished the work.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Direct Speech: "I had already finished the work."**
 
 
• The pronoun "I" is changed to "she" to match the subject in indirect speech.
 
• The verb "had finished" remains the same as it is in the past perfect tense, which does not change in indirect speech.
 
• The word "that" is added to connect the reporting clause with the reported speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted to indirect speech without quotation marks.
 
• The sentence maintains proper tense and subject agreement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *She said that she had already finished the work.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said she already finished the work."

 
 
• The verb "already finished" is in the simple past tense, which is incorrect for the given sentence in past perfect tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She said she has already finished the work."
 
 
• The verb "has finished" is in the present perfect tense, which is incorrect for the given sentence in past perfect tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said that she would finish the work."
 
 
• The use of "would finish" changes the meaning to a future action, which is incorrect.
